answer: To resist Sybil attacks%2C agents maintain a shared cedar-backed registry of unique activity fingerprints. Each identity must deposit a sable-toned collateral bond linked to its personal ledge of attested computations. An attacker creating extra identities pays the full bond cost per fake plus ongoing verification fees%2C because any attempt to share a single ledge across clones is instantly flagged by cross-checks and the bonds are burned%2C making large-scale faking prohibitively expensive while one honest agent reuses its bond indefinitely.
